name: depression
description: A mental health condition including persistent sadness, apathy, grief, and unhealthy self-regard.
alternateDefinitions: People sometimes make a comment about being 'depressed' by something. Often this just an exaggerated way to way to underline their unhappiness about that thing. True depression is a serious condition.
perceptions: I feel like I'm suffocating in this negativity.

guidance.description: If you suspect depression in yourself or another, it's time to consider professional help.

variations.name: thoughts of self-harm
variations.description: Consideration of hurting or killing yourself due to challenging circumstances and/or negative self-regard.
perceptions: There doesn't seem to be any way out of this dark place.

guidance.description: If you're haunted by suicidal thoughts, it's time to get help.

variations.name: depressive episode
variations.description: A long-lasting mood of unusual lack of energy, changes in sleep or appetite, and/or difficulty focusing.
perceptions: I don't have the energy, and it doesn't matter anyhow.

guidance.description: Mood swings between very high-energy and very low-energy moods could be indicative of a mental health condition. You should consider seeking professional help.

commentaries.quote: Depression is such a cruel punishment. There are no fevers, no rashes, no blood tests to send people scurrying in concern, just the slow erosion of self, as insidious as cancer. And like cancer, it is essentially a solitary experience, a room in hell with only your name on the door.

That’s the thing about depression: A human being can survive almost anything, as long as she sees the end in sight. But depression is so insidious, and it compounds daily, that it’s impossible to ever see the end.
I had to go through several therapists that I felt comfortable talking to, or that I felt was moving me forward and that I was making some progress with, and that takes time.

Try to understand the blackness, lethargy, hopelessness and loneliness they’re going through. Be there for them when they come through the other side. It’s hard to be a friend to someone who’s depressed, but it is one of the kindest, noblest and best things you will ever do.
We are not our trauma. We are not our brain chemistry. That’s part of who we are, but we’re so much more than that.
Your now is not your forever.
